answers.how: The apple is about 28 pixels across. Fitting its falling trajectory gives approximately 288 pixels per meter from the known gravity.
The table's vertical extent is about 337 pixels; dividing by approximately 288 pixels per meter gives its height.
The apple moves horizontally about 192 pixels per second near departure; the gravity-derived scale is approximately 288 pixels per meter.
From the table edge to its first floor contact, the apple travels approximately 88 horizontal pixels, using approximately 288 pixels per meter.
At 1.2 seconds, the fitted horizontal and vertical velocities are approximately 192 and 149 pixels per second. Their resultant is converted using approximately 288 pixels per meter.
